title: In defence of the paper map
text: Satellite navigation has made map-reading a dying skill, {{1}} many hikers still refuse to leave home without a paper map. Their reasons are practical rather {{2}} sentimental. Batteries die, signals vanish in valleys, and a folded map never needs charging. More importantly, map-reading builds what psychologists call spatial thinking: the ability to picture landscape {{3}} above. Studies suggest this skill transfers {{4}} other domains, from geometry to packing a car boot. GPS, {{5}} contrast, delivers answers without requiring understanding; follow it blindly and you can be led {{6}} trouble. The wisest approach combines both: navigation devices for speed, the map for judgement. Learn the map, and you will never be completely {{7}} , wherever you wander. That sense of self-reliance, say veteran walkers, is {{8}} makes the paper map worth carrying.
